source_registry.excerpt:
SEC/CFTC Release Nos. 33-11412 and 34-105020; File S7-2026-09; effective March 23, 2026.
Section III.A lists XRP (XRP) among examples of digital commodities.
The release states digital commodities are not themselves securities, but a non-security crypto asset can be offered or sold subject to an investment contract.
The release says it does not supersede or replace the Howey test; the SEC characterizes it as an interpretation of its views and the CFTC provides related guidance.

source_registry.excerpt:
SEC Division of Corporation Finance FAQ updated Nov 2, 2026.
The FAQ answers represent staff views, are not a rule, regulation or Commission statement, have no legal force or effect, and do not alter applicable law.
Q1.4: Whether broad-based governance participants are a group is a facts-and-circumstances determination; participants generally are not a group if unaffiliated and without an agreement, arrangement or understanding to act in concert.
Q1.5: A central party may control participation at protocol, validator or user level, including unilateral power to grant or limit access, change voting processes, control validators, modify rules-based code, reverse transactions or revoke access.
Q2.6: A secondary-market trading platform is a promoter only if it meets the Securities Act Rule 405 promoter definition.

sec_cftc_interpretation.agency_weight: SEC Commission interpretation with related CFTC guidance; not a statute. The release says the Commission may refine, revise or expand its interpretation after public feedback.
